title: Performance issue after upgrade from 3.5 to 4.4
body:
Since we have update from Neo4j 3.5 to 4.4 we have some performance issues.

We think there is a problem in the query planner, used the wrong index.
Is makes the whole database slowdown.

- Neo4j version: 4.4.28
- Operating system:  Ubuntu 23.10

Query:

```
PROFILE MATCH (hour:Hour{Hash: "31138173/2022/12/27/09"})
WITH hour
MATCH (prev:Hour{TimeTree: "31138173"})
WHERE prev.HourInDay < hour.HourInDay
WITH prev, hour
ORDER BY prev.HourInDay DESC LIMIT 1
MERGE (prev)-[:NEXT]->(hour)
```

Run on Neo4j 3.5:

![plan](https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/assets/9036151/91bfff40-0f5e-4b13-9563-083baba6b65b)

Run on Neo4j 4.4.28:

![plan (1)](https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/assets/9036151/2889cb86-2881-4fc7-9323-46ef1156a896)

When we change the query:

```
PROFILE MATCH (hour:Hour{Hash: "31138173/2022/12/27/09"})
WITH hour, hour.HourInDay as notInUsed
MATCH (prev:Hour{TimeTree: "31138173"})
WHERE prev.HourInDay < hour.HourInDay
WITH prev, hour
ORDER BY prev.HourInDay DESC LIMIT 1
MERGE (prev)-[:NEXT]->(hour)
```

Then the query is so mutch better and faster, (same as 3.5):

![plan (2)](https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/assets/9036151/4126c100-a259-4592-bb34-01112cdaab8d)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@reporter 

Affected queries must have:
1. A MATCH clause with multiple components (i.e. comma-separated patterns without a connecting relationship). `MATCH (hour:Hour), (prev:Hour)`  would be an example, but `MATCH (hour:Hour) MATCH (prev:Hour)` and `MATCH (hour:Hour) WITH hour MATCH (prev:Hour)` are also equivalent from the planner perspective, so they also fit. Using one of the previously mentioned workarounds invalidates this condition.
2. Multiple index-compatible predicates like `prev.TimeTree = "31138173" AND prev.HourInDay < hour.HourInDay`.
3. At least one of these predicates must depend on a variable from the other component (`hour` in this case).

Given these conditions, planner currently relies on a heuristic that always chooses to use an index that solves the predicate with dependency (`prev.HourInDay < hour.HourInDay`) over alternatives.

The fix is to consider all index options and choose the one that is optimal according to our cardinality-cost model instead of using a heuristic.
